arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious DNS Tunneling via High-Volume TXT Queries
description: Detects potential DNS tunneling by identifying hosts making excessive TXT record queries to a single domain.
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryType: 16  # TXT record
  by_domain:
    GroupBy: QueryName
    Condition: selection | count() by QueryName > 300 within 60s
  by_host:
    GroupBy: SrcIp
    Condition: selection | count() by SrcIp > 500 within 60s
  filter:
    - QueryName|endswith: '.local'
    - QueryName|endswith: '.arpa'
  condition: by_domain and by_host and not filter
level: high
references:

level: high
references:

description: Detects phishing-driven PowerShell execution via Outlook.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike beacon configuration in memory or traffic"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $xormagic = { 0x55 0x8B 0xEC 0x83 0xEC ?? 0x8B 0x45 ?? 0x85 0xC0 0x74 ?? 0x8B 0x4D ?? 0x85 0xC9 0x74 }
        $cfgmagic = "beacon" ascii wide
    condition:
        $xormagic at 0 and $cfgmagic in (0..0x1000)
}

arguments.summary: A low-severity port scan alert from 10.0.5.14 to 10.0.4.1 triggered initial detection. Further correlation revealed that the source IP (10.0.5.14) was misattributed; the true compromised host was WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), a high-criticality finance workstation. The incident involved a phishing-initiated compromise via malicious Outlook attachment, leading to execution of encoded PowerShell, loading of an unsigned DLL (Cobalt Strike beacon), and C2 communication to a known-bad IP (198.51.100.23). Lateral movement via SMB was attempted toward WS-FIN-050. Despite initial low confidence, the event was part of a coordinated post-exploitation sequence. Full EDR and SIEM telemetry confirmed the attack chain. A full endpoint scan detected a Linux dropper, though unrelated to the primary threat vector.
